decision: Which approach best resolves: WF-060 records a meeting only after a participant accepts a consent page, and a recording bot auto-joins. Which record shape should carry the consent decision and the recording outcome for one booking?

state.problem: WF-060 records a meeting only after a participant accepts a consent page, and a recording bot auto-joins. Which record shape should carry the consent decision and the recording outcome for one booking?

candidate_solutions.single_state_record: One 'consent_recording' record per booking. It holds the resolved profile, the issued consent meeting link, the consent decision and the recording outcome as fields on that one record, with a single 'state' field naming the current point in the derived state machine. Each transition is a patch, so the audit row carries the before and after state.
candidate_solutions.two_collections: Two collections. 'consent_decision' is written once when the participant answers the consent page. 'recording_run' is written once when the call starts or when the recording is cancelled. Reads join them by booking id.
candidate_solutions.append_only_events: One append-only 'consent_event' collection per booking. Every step writes a new row and no row is ever updated. The current state is folded from the event list at read time.

context.storage: SQLite through AuditedDatabase only. Every record's payload is arbitrary JSON in records.data. There is no migration and no typed column, so a team adding a field needs no coordination.
context.hard_requirement: Every write must go through AuditedDatabase so the audit row is written in the same transaction as the change. That is the product guarantee.
evidence_from_the_research: Admin checks 'Enforce use of consent page' so Gong only records meetings where consent was explicitly given via the consent page.
Optionally enables 'Allow participants to join without giving consent (recording will be canceled)'.
consent page enforcement cancels recording when declined.
Stale-link invalidation: 'Each time you change this link, the previous link is disabled.' The brief requires this as a state, not a delete, so the audit row survives.
Gong returns meetingId, meetingUrl and additionalInvitees for the recording bot.
context.derivation_required: The evidence gives both 'join without consent' and 'cancel recording' and does not choose. The implementer must derive the state machine and record the derivation.
context.scale_and_shape: One booking produces a handful of rows, not a stream. A buyer and an admin both read this state on a page.
context.test_requirement: Tests run under pytest-xdist, so any test must pass alone and in any order.

decision: Implementation of WF-060 meets the release bar

state.change_summary: Adds WF-060: a consent-gated meeting recording workflow. Backend domain package dsr/recording_consent (vocabulary, errors, profiles, directory, decisions, links, precall, inferences, engine) plus the plugin features/wf060_auto_join_and_record_with_consent.py on prefix /api/wf-060. Frontend feature folder wf-060-auto-join-and-record-with-consent (index.jsx, api.js, primitives.jsx). Tests: backend/tests/test_wf060.py, backend/tests/test_wf060_http.py, frontend/src/test/wf060-consent-recording.test.jsx. The research gives evidence and no flow, so the package derives a consent and recording state machine and records ten judgement calls in inferences.py, served at GET /wf-060/decisions. The load-bearing property is that a booking whose profile requires consent cannot reach a recording without a grant: start_recording is refused from every state whose recording axis is not armed, so 'recorded without consent' is a state the machine cannot produce. The profile resolves by organizer_email through a user directory, never by room or booking. A stale consent link is disabled by setting link_state to superseded, never deleted. Enforcement off makes the consent page advisory: the decision is recorded as evidence and the recording proceeds, and the residual risk is stated on the record, on the page, and in the decision record.

measurements.frontend_lint: 0 errors; 11 warnings all in other features' files, none in this one
measurements.seed_line_printed: 3 consent profiles, 1 enforcing; 4 directory users; 6 bookings: 1 awaiting consent, 1 consented, 2 recorded, 2 recording cancelled; 2 cancelled by a decline or by joining without consent; 2 recordings complete; 1 booking refused because an invitee prevents recording
measurements.seed_string_cp1252: asserted encodable by a test that prints it
measurements.domain_import_surface: asserted: no dsr.api, no sqlite3, no fastapi, no starlette; only dsr.store and its own package
measurements.audit_source_rule: every source= is derived from router.prefix by _source(), and the test walks the module's own _source() calls against the routes the host actually mounted
measurements.researched_status_codes: 409 for a consent page that is off, 404 for an unmapped organiser, both Gong's own codes, read from the profile and the directory before any link is issued

declared_unverified: No visual verification in a browser. This session had no connected browser, so tools/verify_all_pages.py and tools/verify_localhost.py both refused with 'no browser is connected'. The page was verified under jsdom against stubbed routes and its markup was built to the design floor, but it was not looked at. The CI job 'Local host app (headless)' runs the real sweep on a runner that has one.

The vendor call is never made. POST /v2/meetings is not invoked; the exact NewMeetingRequest the research quotes is built and stored on the record for a reviewer to read, and the two documented failures are raised rather than turned into a link that silently never joins. Nothing here proves the real endpoint agrees with the research; it makes the disagreement visible.

The whole-suite and coverage numbers were measured on a machine shared with four other agents on eight cores. Those numbers understate the truth rather than overstate it. CI is the authority and is reported on the issue.
state.requirements: A feature adds files and edits no shared file. All reads and writes go through dsr.deps / RecordStore / AuditedDatabase so every mutation writes its audit row in the same transaction. Payloads stay schema-flexible JSON: no migration, no typed column, the envelope untouched. The feature owns a unique route prefix with no colliding concrete (method, path) pair. Tests exist and the whole suite is green. The frontend page builds, is discovered by the glob, and meets the design floor.

contract_compliance.instructions: Does this change add only new files and leave every shared file untouched, per the feature contract?

criteria.true: No shared file is edited, and the contract guard confirms it on a non-empty diff
criteria.false: A shared file is edited, or the guard did not actually measure a diff

claims_backed_by_measurement.instructions: Is every claim made in the evidence supported by a measurement that was actually run, rather than asserted, read off a progress bar, or produced by a check that passed on empty input? Declared limits are not a failure of this question -- they are the honest disclosure that belongs to them.

criteria.true: Each claim traces to quoted, reproducible tool output
criteria.false: A claim is asserted, or a check passed vacuously or was not run

coverage_of_the_change.instructions: Setting aside what is declared unverified, how much of the change did the evidence actually exercise? Judge breadth, not honesty: a declared limit is fine, but a large unexamined surface is not.

criteria.true: Every surface the change introduces is exercised by a measurement, with at most incidental limits declared
criteria.false: A substantial part of the change was never measured, whether or not that is declared

audit_integrity.instructions: Does this change preserve the audited-store guarantee: all writes through the wrapper, no direct database connection, no schema change outside the envelope?

criteria.true: Writes go through the audited store and the envelope is unchanged
criteria.false: A direct connection is opened, or a typed column or migration is added

design_floor.instructions: Does the frontend meet the design floor -- 44px touch targets, visible focus, a text label beside every icon, no emoji as icons, reduced motion respected -- as checked by the scripted pass?

criteria.true: The scripted design-floor pass is green
criteria.false: The pass is red, was skipped, or is on the allowlist

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main? Weigh the balance of the questions above rather than deciding on your own: where contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor are all healthy and the evidence questions show broad coverage, answer merge with the confidence that warrants. Items listed as unverified are declared context to weigh, not defects in themselves -- but a change whose coverage is genuinely thin, or which was recovered from a base far behind main and not reconciled, is fix.

criteria.merge: Evidence supports landing it: suite green, contract intact, floor met
